newsitem.title: USA: IBM to acquire insurance software firm.
newsitem.headline: IBM to acquire insurance software firm.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp said on Monday it has reached an agreement to acquire Professional Data Management Associates Inc, a private software and services company, for undisclosed terms.
IBM said the deal will strengthen its position to provide business solutions for the global insurance industry.

A key factor in the acquitision was PDM's LifePRO, an online system for life and annuity insurance processing, IBM said. In addition to supporting both individual and group-policy administration, LifePRO helps companies reduce operating and overhead costs and eliminate multiple administration systems.

IBM said it intends to operate PDM as a wholly-owned subsidiary through December 31, 1996. PDM will be merged with IBM on January 1, 1997 and all PDM employees will become employees of IBM's Worldwide Insurance Solutions.

IBM will offer LifePRO as its multiple platform solution life insurance software package to its insurance company customers. IBM will develop versions of the software to run on the System 390 mainframe. IBM also intends to offer future versions on the AS/400 minicomputer line and for the Windows NT operating system.
